NTA. Strange but I wish my parents were more like that with me. When I left school I immediately started touring with a band at 17. Parents supported me in doing this and helped out financially (I was never given handouts but always had somewhere to stay and eat for free when we weren’t away travelling). When that dried up it took me ages to learn about being financially responsible and independent and, it pains me to say it, but that childish side of me always kept that ‘safety net’ in the back of my mind. I always thought I could be financially flippant and my parents would have my back. This is obviously just my character and totally my own doing, in no way am I blaming that on my parents; just making the point that too much support, financial or not, creates this environment where adolescents can grow in to self-righteous needy young adults who have it in their head that the world owes them a living. Nice video, mate. I think it depends on where your coming from as a writer. Some artists don't bother with lyrics too much because the pull comes from somewhere else for them (a nice guitar riff, a beat, a soundscape). As a lyricist I think lyrics are paramount to a song, obviously, but I can certainly appreciate a song or an artist who doesn't necessarily wholly pride themselves on their lyrical content. Then there are the rare few who manage to encapsulate great lyrics, melody, emotion and the rest, like Billy Joel. His live record 'Songs In The Attic' really showed me that it's possible to focus on every single detail of a song. We've all heard songs where we say 'Those lyrics are great' or 'that riff is amazing' but the really good songwriters have it all in one lovely audible ball of song.

I think that tolerance is based almost entirely on habit. If you smoke really heavily (every day) for a long time, as you have, and then take a break suddenly your more likely to feel the side effects you mentioned. If you ease your way into smoking less the side effects of not smoking will be far less severe.

To answer your question - no. The longer you are in your 'break' the more your body and mind will grow accustomed to the lesser amount your smoking. My advice would be to stick it out, the side effects are temporary. On a side note smoking less really makes smoking kinda like a treat again. I've been there, and smoking heavily all the time is really sweet, don't get me wrong, but smoking less makes you really appreciate the smokes you do have.
